experiments.name: Team EPA + individual QB
experiments.mechanism: Team EPA already reflects QB play. An extra full QB effect can repeat information embedded in team efficiency.

experiments.name: EPA/QB + protection
experiments.mechanism: Sacks and QB hits affect team EPA and QB results. Adding their standalone effect again can repeat protection-related information.

experiments.name: EPA + turnovers
experiments.mechanism: Interceptions and lost fumbles already affect EPA. A separate full turnover effect may duplicate their impact.

experiments.name: Adjusted EPA + schedule correction
experiments.mechanism: Opponent-adjusted ratings already account for opponents. An additional standalone schedule adjustment can reapply related information.

experiments.name: Home-aware baseline + home bonus
experiments.mechanism: The exact home/neutral indicator is already a baseline feature. Adding it again is a deliberately constructed duplicate-column control.

experiments.name: Total EPA + pass/run efficiency
experiments.mechanism: Total efficiency and its pass/run matchup components share information. Only incremental matchup information should earn an extra effect.

experiments.name: EPA + current rest (comparison)
experiments.mechanism: Current rest is not explicitly in this baseline. This comparison checks that the procedure does not automatically call every extra input a duplicate.

method: Fit a baseline on earlier games. Learn the added signal’s standalone points effect separately, with no second intercept.
Project the signal onto baseline inputs with training-only weighted least squares. This measures linear predictability, not causal attribution.
Compare baseline + full standalone effect with baseline + a newly learned effect of only the unprojected signal. Baseline coefficients stay fixed.
Correlated inputs are not automatically double counted; reparameterizing an unregularized joint linear model alone cannot create an edge.
Full-add is an intentionally constructed overlap stress test, not a reconstruction of any sportsbook’s model.
Market alignment uses only games where new-only minus full-add is at least one point in magnitude, chosen without target outcomes. It is a directional diagnostic, not an executable betting rule.
Approximate intervals resample weekly blocks and adjust for 21 current-audit checks. Earlier inspected research and all future selection choices still require an untouched final test.

deferred.name: New injury penalty versus absence already in recent results
deferred.needed: Timestamped lineup/availability snapshots and role/usage history. The 2025 injury archive lacks publication/modification times.

deferred.name: Weather-adjusted baseline plus another weather penalty
deferred.needed: Archived pregame forecast timestamps and an explicit record of what the baseline already includes; realized weather is insufficient.

deferred.name: Travel/fatigue rating plus separate rest penalty
deferred.needed: A documented fatigue baseline, travel itinerary/venue history, and timestamped inputs. Current rest-only comparison is not that model.

limits: QB identity remains a previous-game proxy, not a verified announced starter.
Historical EPA is from current source vintages; source revision effects remain.
Archived line times and bookmaker inputs are unknown. This audit cannot prove that Vegas duplicates an adjustment.
